label: a house maid in her black dress, white apron and cap, 1900s
note: Gathered 2026-11-07 for T-3448, the 1904 house maid's dress first worn by Mary Reynolds of the Glessner household. Both are staged comic stereographs, neither of Chicago, the Glessner house or Mary Reynolds, and both are monochrome. Kelley's 1904 maid at a front door gives the whole outfit; Graves's maid seen from behind gives the back of the apron and a lighter working shirtwaist. A reference set says what a woman of this role and decade looked like, never what Mary Reynolds wore on a given day.
